# Jira DC→Cloud Migration Readiness Assessment — Kickoff Notes

- **Client:** Harbourline Freight (logistics, ~380 Jira users)
- **Call:** 24/9 — attendees: Aoife Brennan (their PM), Marek (Jira admin), me
- **Scope:** Jira **Data Center → Cloud** ONLY. Confluence is out of scope for now.
- Next call: Friday 2/10

## Decisions

- Confluence is **out of scope** for now — Jira only.
- Inactivity cutoff for the user review is **24 months** (no login in 24 months) — **Aoife's requirement**, not 12.
- **Project leads are never dropped** — even if inactive, they own project/issue data. They are protected from removal.
- Deliverables: a **readiness report + PDF for Aoife**, plus **scripts we can rerun**.
- Next call: **Friday 2/10**.

## Actions (with owner)

| Action | Owner |
|---|---|
| Produce the readiness report + PDF for Aoife | Me |
| Provide reusable scripts (rerunnable against the DC instance) | Me |
| Archive assessment for ~3–4 dead projects | Me (to propose), Marek (executes) |
| User hygiene: identify junk/dupe/no-email accounts | Me |
| Standard vs Premium decision — bring numbers to the decision | Me |
| Deep-dive the FRT project (~70k issues) | Me |
| Prepare for Friday 2/10 call | All |

## Open questions

- Standard vs Premium plan — Aoife wants **numbers** before deciding (headcount-based estimate).
- FRT project ~70k issues — is it one plan that caps it, or should it be split up / thinned?
- Which exact projects to archive? Marek thinks 3–4 can go; need to confirm each is actually dead.
- Users with **no email at all** — are these the contractor/integration accounts? Should they be retained?
- Service accounts for integrations — which, and how are they mapped / retained post-migration?
